front: What is hoisting?
back: JS moves declarations to the top of their scope. var is initialized as undefined; let/const are in the temporal dead zone until their declaration.

front: What is a pure function?
back: Same input → same output, and no side effects.

front: What does React's key prop actually do?
back: It tells React how to match children between renders so it can preserve state and DOM instead of unmounting/remounting.

front: Difference between position: absolute and fixed?
back: absolute is positioned relative to the nearest positioned ancestor; fixed is positioned relative to the viewport.

front: TypeScript: any vs unknown?
back: any opts out of the type system; unknown is a safe top type that requires narrowing before use.

front: What's the difference between <section> and <div>?
back: <section> is a semantic landmark representing a thematic grouping of content, typically with a heading; <div> carries no semantic meaning and is purely a styling/grouping hook.

front: When should you use alt="" versus real alt text?
back: alt="" for purely decorative images with no informational value, so screen readers skip them; real descriptive alt text for images that convey information.

front: What's the CSS cascade's tie-breaking order?
back: Importance (!important) > specificity (id > class > element) > source order (later rules win when specificity ties).

front: What does `gap` do in a flex or grid container?
back: Sets consistent spacing between flex/grid items without needing margin hacks on individual children.

front: What's the temporal dead zone?
back: The period between entering a scope and a let/const declaration's actual line, during which the variable exists but accessing it throws a ReferenceError.

front: What's the difference between == and ===?
back: == performs type coercion before comparing; === compares both value and type without coercion.

front: What's the difference between any and unknown?
back: any disables type checking entirely; unknown accepts any value but forces a narrowing check before you can use it.

front: What does a discriminated union look like?
back: A union of object types that share a common literal field (e.g. `kind`), letting TypeScript narrow reliably by switching on that field.

front: Why does the useEffect dependency array matter?
back: It tells React when to re-run the effect; an incomplete array causes stale closures, an unnecessary one causes extra re-runs.

front: What's the difference between controlled and uncontrolled components?
back: Controlled components have their value driven by React state (value + onChange); uncontrolled components manage their own internal DOM state, read via a ref.

front: What's the difference between git merge and git rebase?
back: merge creates a new commit joining two histories, preserving both branches' commit history; rebase replays your commits on top of another branch, producing a linear history.

front: What causes a merge conflict?
back: Git can't automatically reconcile changes because both branches modified the same lines (or one deleted what the other modified).

front: What does an HTTP 401 vs 403 status code mean?
back: 401 Unauthorized means authentication is missing or invalid; 403 Forbidden means you're authenticated but not allowed to access this resource.

front: What's the difference between PUT and PATCH?
back: PUT replaces the entire resource with the provided representation; PATCH applies a partial update to specific fields.

front: What does 'arrange-act-assert' mean?
back: A structuring convention for a test: set up inputs (arrange), call the code (act), check the result (assert).

front: Why does React Testing Library favor getByRole over getByTestId?
back: getByRole matches how assistive technology perceives the page, so it doubles as a lightweight accessibility check; getByTestId doesn't.

front: What is the 'first rule of ARIA'?
back: Use a native HTML element with the semantics you need instead of re-purposing an element and patching it with ARIA.

front: Why shouldn't you remove a focus outline without replacing it?
back: It's the only visual indicator a keyboard user has for where they currently are on the page.

front: Why can't a token in localStorage be trusted the way an httpOnly cookie can?
back: localStorage is readable by any JavaScript on the page, including an attacker's script from an XSS vulnerability; httpOnly cookies are invisible to JavaScript entirely.

front: What does CSRF actually exploit?
back: The browser's automatic attachment of a site's cookies to any request addressed to that site, regardless of which page initiated the request.

front: What do LCP, INP, and CLS each measure?
back: LCP: how long the largest visible element takes to render. INP: responsiveness to user interactions. CLS: how much visible content unexpectedly shifts during load.

front: Why should you wrap the whole app in one error boundary?
back: You shouldn't — a single top-level boundary means any failure anywhere blanks the whole page; scope boundaries around individual risky sections instead.

front: What's the difference between a Server Component and a Client Component in Next.js?
back: Server Components run only on the server and never ship code to the browser; Client Components ('use client') run in the browser and support hooks and interactivity.

front: What's the tradeoff of SSG compared to SSR?
back: SSG serves extremely fast, cheaply-hosted static content, but it's only as fresh as the last build; SSR renders fresh per request at the cost of server compute.

front: What does the <button type="submit"> default to inside a <form> if type is omitted?
back: "submit" -- an unspecified <button> inside a form defaults to type="submit", which is a common source of accidental form submissions.

front: What's the difference between <ol> and <ul>?
back: <ol> is for ordered/sequential content where order matters (steps, rankings); <ul> is for unordered collections where order is incidental.

front: What's the difference between visibility: hidden and display: none?
back: visibility: hidden hides the element but it still takes up layout space; display: none removes it from the layout entirely.

front: What does `flex-shrink: 0` do?
back: Prevents a flex item from shrinking below its base size when the container doesn't have enough room, even as siblings shrink.

front: What's the difference between em and rem units?
back: em is relative to the current element's (or its parent's) font size; rem is always relative to the root element's font size, avoiding compounding.

front: Why can margin-top on a child sometimes visually apply to its parent instead?
back: Margin collapsing -- adjacent vertical margins between a parent and its first/last child can collapse together unless the parent has padding, a border, or overflow set.

front: What's the difference between null and undefined?
back: undefined means a variable has been declared but not assigned a value; null is an explicit, intentional assignment representing 'no value'.

front: What does Array.prototype.map return compared to forEach?
back: map returns a new array built from the callback's return values; forEach returns undefined and is used purely for side effects.

front: What's a closure?
back: A function that retains access to variables from its enclosing scope even after that outer function has finished executing.

front: What does the spread operator do when copying an object?
back: Creates a shallow copy -- top-level properties are copied by value, but nested objects/arrays are still shared by reference.

front: What does `interface Admin extends User` do?
back: Extends the User interface, inheriting all its fields while allowing Admin to add its own additional fields.

front: What's a type guard?
back: A function or check that narrows a broader type to a more specific one within a conditional block, e.g. `typeof x === 'string'`.

front: What does `keyof` do?
back: Produces a union of an object type's own property names as string literal types, useful for constraining generic key parameters.

front: Why does React warn about missing 'key' props in a list?
back: Keys let React match array items across renders to correctly preserve, update, or discard component state instead of re-creating everything.

front: What's the difference between useMemo and useCallback?
back: useMemo memoizes a computed value; useCallback memoizes a function reference itself, useful for stable callback identity in dependency arrays.

front: Why must hooks be called unconditionally at the top level?
back: React tracks hooks by call order across renders; conditionally skipping a hook call shifts that order and breaks state tracking for subsequent hooks.

front: What does `git stash` do?
back: Temporarily shelves uncommitted changes so you can switch branches cleanly, then reapply them later with `git stash pop`.

front: What's the difference between `git fetch` and `git pull`?
back: fetch downloads remote changes without merging them into your working branch; pull does a fetch followed by an automatic merge (or rebase).

front: What does an HTTP 429 status code mean?
back: Too Many Requests -- the client has been rate-limited and should back off before retrying.

front: What's idempotency in the context of HTTP methods?
back: An idempotent request produces the same result no matter how many times it's repeated; GET, PUT, and DELETE are idempotent, POST generally is not.

front: What does 'mocking too much' risk in an integration test?
back: If you mock the exact logic you're trying to verify, the test can pass even when that logic is broken -- it stops proving anything real.

front: Why prefer userEvent over fireEvent for simulating typing?
back: userEvent simulates the fuller, more realistic sequence of real keystrokes and focus behavior, closer to what an actual user does.

front: What's the difference between aria-label and aria-labelledby?
back: aria-label supplies an accessible name directly as a string; aria-labelledby points to another element's id whose text becomes the name.

front: Why do landmark elements like <main> and <nav> matter?
back: They let screen reader users jump directly between page regions instead of reading through everything sequentially.

front: What's the difference between authentication and authorization?
back: Authentication verifies who you are (login); authorization determines what you're allowed to do once identified.

front: Why can't Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * be combined with credentialed requests?
back: Browsers explicitly disallow it, since that combination would let any site read authenticated responses on a user's behalf.

front: What does memoization actually trade off?
back: It trades extra memory (caching a result) for avoiding repeated expensive computation or re-renders -- not free, so it shouldn't be applied everywhere by default.

front: Why is code splitting useful for large apps?
back: It breaks the JS bundle into smaller chunks loaded on demand, so users only download the code needed for the page they're actually viewing.

front: What is ISR (Incremental Static Regeneration)?
back: Pages are statically generated but can be regenerated in the background after a set interval, without a full site rebuild.

front: Why do layouts persist across navigation in the Next.js App Router?
back: Shared layout.tsx files wrap nested routes without re-rendering on navigation between pages that share them, preserving state like scroll position or an open menu.
